ai_industry.content_original:
A Look at Some of Our Favorite Cinematic Suite Tools in Topview’s Film Studio 2.0
If you're checking out Topview’s Film Studio for the first time, here’s a breakdown of our picks for the most helpful AI tools in the cinematic suite.
The film and video landscape is changing rapidly, and whether you love it or hate it, if you want to keep up with this new AI frontier, this might be one of the best places to start.
As we covered in the intro piece, Topview is more than an AI clip tool; it’s a platform for those interested in AI filmmaking itself, or in finding ways to use AI tools to assist with traditional filmmaking processes.
To dive deeper, we’ve picked out some of our favorite AI tools from Topview’s Film Studio, Cinematic Suite, which offer filmmakers more than random clips; they can develop and even direct their own cinematic projects.
Exploring Topview’s Film Studio Cinematic Suite
As you can see in our video breakdown, we got to explore the Topview platform and dive into the Film Studio, which might be the best place for filmmakers to try out different AI tools and workflows.
Topview’s Film Studio 2.0 offers a wide range of tools in its cinematic suite and other film skills in its library that can help filmmakers and artists create complete AI films with connected stories, consistent characters, and shot-by-shot creative control, all on one easy-to-navigate canvas.
We’ll get into the specific tools we dove into a bit more below, but if you’re checking it out for the first time, it’s worth noting that the cinematic suite is growing, and there are 25+ tools in the cinematic suite now, including visual style modifiers, storyboard previews, and full-scale 3D builders, along with hundreds of Film Skills, including director controls, action sequences, and director-inspired looks.
Once you dive into the platform, you can also create your own Film Skills to easily replicate your favorite scenes, workflows, or moves.
Our Top Cinematic Suite Tools
Now, moving on to some of our favorite tools we tried in the Cinematic Suite, we want to highlight the following five tools as helpful for those exploring these AI filmmaking workflows for the first time.
Actor Expression Enhancer
Credit: Topview
Perhaps the most interesting tool in the Cinematic Suite, it solves one of the most common issues we see with AI films and videos: the acting and performance of these AI characters. They’re often flat, odd, or uncanny.
This tool is a helpful, direct way to work on these AI performances by letting users give specific directions and make major to minor adjustments. You can change subtle reactions, adjust eyelines, or aim to help them hit and land their emotional beats better.
Clip Edit
Credit: Topview
A more basic tool that can be most helpful for those with video editing backgrounds, as it is a simple way to hone in on one clip or part of your project without needing to regenerate your whole film.
The Clip Edit tool also now has an Edit with Masks feature, which we’ve enjoyed exploring, and it can be an even better way to dive deeper and make granular changes to your clips while saving time and resources.
3D Builder
Credit: Topview
One of the more ambitious, and certainly deep and complex, tools in the Cinematic Suite is the 3D Builder, which lets you completely rearrange your scenes, block subjects, move your camera around, and then test all these spatial relationships in 3D before you generate.
It’s quite sophisticated and worth exploring further, especially if you have a background and interest in 3D design and modeling and want an interface that lets you make very precise moves and sequences.
Storyboard Preview
Credit: Topview
For those coming into Topview’s Film Studio with little to no AI video experience, this could be a good first tool to try, as it shows how AI filmmaking has evolved over the past year or so.
Most workflows for artists in this space start with image generation and storyboards because, as you can guess, they are the easiest to control, the most cost-efficient in terms of generation resources, and most helpful for defining your characters, shots, and moves—similar to how actual filmmaking works.
Film Genre Skills
Credit: Topview
Finally, the Film Genre Skills tool is one of the most fun to explore for inspiration, with over 200 built-in film style skills already added to the platform. You’ll obviously recognize many of these, and many have been shared online in the past.
But if you have a cinematic style in mind that goes with a genre you’re trying to work in, whether you ultimately use these generations for your final projects or just as stylistic inspiration, this could be a good tool to explore and play around with the style, look, and overall aesthetic of your video.
More to Come
These are our top picks for tools in the Cinematic Suite that we found most interesting to explore. You can obviously try many more yourself and see which ones are most intriguing and helpful for your own workflows.
Stay tuned for the next installment in our series, where we create a full AI micro film from start to finish.

ai_industry.title: Mistral’s New ‘Le Chonk’ AI Model Is Big, Open and Now Available for Download
ai_industry.summary_original: Mistral Large 4 is a state-of-the-art model for cyberdefense, manufacturing, finance-related tasks and multimodal use.
ai_industry.content_original:
New AI models are coming, and they don’t stop coming.
On the heels of the recent rollouts of Meta’s Muse and Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon, Mistral AI is launching its new flagship frontier model, Mistral Large 4. The model – affectionately known as “Le Chonk” – was available in public preview earlier this month. Now, after weeks of additional reinforcement learning, fine-tuning and assessing it with feedback from developers, cybersecurity experts and state officials, the Mistral team announced Thursday that ML4 is available for download.
“The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations,” Mistral said in its announcement. “We’ve put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity.”
More from CNET
A French company known for its open-source and open-weight LLMs, Mistral AI reports that the Large 4 model “ranks among the best open-weight models of the world” on aggregated metrics and also outperforms European and US models, while also catching up to Chinese competitors, who have been dominating the open-weight sector.
Earlier this month, I spoke with Mistral Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and VP of Science Pierre Stock about the new model – what they’re calling the best open model built in the West – and its specialized capabilities and extreme compute efficiency. Here’s what to know.
Key capabilities of Mistral Large 4
Lample and Stock said that Mistral Large 4 was built to process both text and images, closing performance gaps from previous Mistral models. Specifically, Large 4 touts more advanced cybersecurity and agentic capabilities, as well as a better ability to handle manufacturing- and finance-related tasks.
Cybersecurity
Mistral Large 4 was designed to excel at defensive cybersecurity tasks, including log inspection, code auditing and checking for newly published exploits or vulnerabilities. Beyond defensive measures, Mistral says the new model offers offensive cybersecurity measures to identify and address weaknesses.
Agentic AI
“Really, the core competency we’re looking at for ML4 is agentic capabilities,” Stock said.
Mistral Large 4 was built with a focus on agentic performance for planning, research or handling complex enterprise tasks that would take human experts hours or days to complete. The Mistral AI team said the model reaches “state-of-the-art” performance on critical agentic benchmarks like SWE-bench and Terminal Bench – evaluation frameworks for testing how well agents handle complex tasks – for tasks like coding, analyzing and pulling requests.
Geospatial and grounding capabilities
Mistral says the model outperforms competitors in aerial and satellite imagery analysis, with the capacity to identify visual patterns and objects on maps, such as forest fires.
“On grounding capabilities, it outperforms all existing models, including the closed ones,” Mistral said when it released the model preview. “These are critical as cyberattacks get faster and cheaper, companies write more code than ever and the world needs more chips to keep up with AI demand.”
Grounding is a technique used in AI development to try to eliminate hallucinations – when the LLM generates inaccurate information – by anchoring the AI’s outputs in external resources, like documents and databases, rather than just the materials it was trained on internally. Grounding also helps keep data and information fresh while providing context for the AI’s responses.
Mistral says the new model was also trained on more than 160 languages, including every official language of the European Union, as well as Latin and non-Latin languages, to answer prompts natively.
If you’re interested in getting started with ML4, it’s available to try and customize in Mistral Studio, through the Mistral API, or on OpenRouter. Mistral also says you can download the open weights from Hugging Face, try ML4 in Vibe Code or access it through Nvidia-hosted endpoints, with additional options to customize for enterprise users.

ai_industry.title: Post-training 4B model with RL to fly Tesla Roadster 21% better than GPT-6 Astra
ai_industry.summary_original: We RL-trained Qwen3-4B to fly a simulated flying Roadster. In storms, it beats DeepSeek, Muse, Beam, Nemotron and GPT-6 Astra, even when they get unlimited time to think.
ai_industry.content_original:
Last Thursday (October 15), Tesla's new Roadster drove off a ramp that curled over until the car was upside down, rolled upright in the air and landed. It then used thrusters to hop over a Cybertruck. Turns out the future does have flying cars.
The demo had already been pushed back two weeks, "due to high winds" (Elon Musk on X). That made us wonder: with a language model in the pilot's seat, how would the car do in that wind?
We built an RL environment around a physics simulator of a flying roadster to find out, handed the controls to LLMs, and turned the wind up. We let some of the latest best models fly it: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Meta's Muse Spark Open, Reflection's Beam 1.0, NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, TypeSafe's Jev 1.14, and even OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.
Asked for decisions in real time, these models crashed almost every flight: most take 1 to 6 s to answer, and the car needs a new action every 0.2 s. When we paused the world so the models could think as long as they wanted, they still lost to a 4B model we trained with RL in a storm.
Storm, 33 m/s wind: DeepSeek, with unlimited time to think, comes down leaning and hits the road with its body. Our RL-trained 4B lands level.
TL;DR
- We built an RL environment around a physics simulator of a flying roadster with four air thrusters, gusty wind and the reveal's two stunts: a ramp flip and a kickflip over a Cybertruck. An LLM flies it with one command every 0.2 s while the car keeps moving.
- The latest open models can't fly it in real time. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Nemotron 3.5 Super, Muse Spark Open and Beam 1.0 take 1 to 6 s per decision and land 0% of kickflips and 3% or less of ramp flips. GPT-6 Astra also lands 0% on the clock.
- RL post-training made a 4B model our best pilot. Qwen3-4B, trained for about $13, answers in 0.09 s and lands 90% of kickflips in real time. With the world paused for the model to think, the best open model, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, lands 87% and the other open models land 58 to 62%. Even GPT-6 Astra lands only 74%.
- Everything is open source, and you can fly your own model without a GPU (Try it).
Watch how the models fly the car. Pick a stunt, a wind level and a model below to replay the same flight on a held-out scene. The full page also shows the pilot decision every 0.2 seconds, the telemetry the model saw, and how long each reply took.
RL environment for flying Tesla Roadster in the wind #
Four air thrusters lift the car, and push it down when it's upside down
The car is a rigid body, 4.5 m long and 2,000 kg dry, simulated at 500 Hz. Lift comes from four cold-gas thrusters at the corners of the floor of the car. Each thruster is good for 12 kN, fed from one tank of compressed air (110 to 170 kg per flight). They push straight out of the floor. If the left pair fires harder, the car rolls, and if the front pair fires harder, it pitches.
When the car is upside down, the same thrusters push it toward the ground, and that is what makes both stunts hard.
A car falling flat or sideways catches far more wind
A car is built to move nose first. When it falls flat, or the wind hits it from the side, it shows five to nine times as much area to the air, so the wind pushes it around far more. Near the road the wind is weaker, and gusts come on top of the average. Each flight gets a mean wind from a random direction, in one of three bands: light (up to 14 m/s), gale (14 to 24 m/s) or storm (24 to 33 m/s).
The wheels can take a 4 m drop, but the roof can't touch the ground
The car can touch the ground with its four sprung wheels or with its body. It counts as a crash when:
Two stunts from the reveal: a ramp flip and a kickflip over a Cybertruck
In the ramp flip, a ramp curls over and the car leaves the deck upside down 10 to 14 m up, then has to roll upright and land. In the kickflip, the car comes in at 50 to 94 km/h, clears a parked Cybertruck, rolls a full 360 degrees and lands.
A flight succeeds only if the car ends up on all four wheels on the 14 m road, within about 20 degrees of level, no longer spinning, and without a crash. Every task randomizes the speed, the air in the tank, the wind and gusts, and the ramp size or truck position. The held-out tasks use seeds that no model trained on.
What the model sees, and what it sends back
At the start of each flight, the model gets a briefing. It describes the car, the crash rules and the five commands it can send, and then the task. Here is the task part of the briefing for one held-out storm flight:
After that, every 0.2 s of simulated time, the model gets one line of telemetry and replies with one JSON object. Here is the line our trained Qwen 4B model saw 1.2 s into that flight, while it was upside down above the truck:
The model replied {"mode": "rotate", "axis": "roll", "to": 360.0, "lift": 1.0} in 0.15 s, which kept the roll going. The whole flight took 19 replies:
The truck part of each line also gives the time until the car reaches the truck and the time until it's past it, at the current speed, so the model doesn't have to do that division itself. Every LLM in this post sees the same lines, and the hand-written pilot below reads the same numbers.
The five commands are coast (all thrusters off), climb (stay level at a given vertical speed), hold (hold a given roll and pitch), rotate (spin about one axis to a total angle, braking to stop on it) and land (level out and come down softly). The model picks one command, with its numbers, in each reply. A flight computer then turns that command into thrust for each of the four thrusters, 50 times a second, until the next reply arrives.
The car doesn't stop while the model thinks
If a model takes 2 s to answer, the car flies ten 0.2 s intervals on the old command before the new one takes over. We time every reply end to end. Only the first decision is untimed, like a plan made before takeoff.
We picked 0.2 s because the kickflip's roll takes about a second and has to start within a few tenths of a second of the right moment. With one second between decisions, no pilot could time it, whether model or script. To separate judgment from speed, we also fly every model a second way, with the simulator paused until each reply arrives, so the model has unlimited time to think.
Half the reward is for a clean landing
For RL the reward runs from 0 to 1. It gives partial credit for height, clearing the truck, rotation and touchdown quality, then 0.4 for a successful landing and 0.1 for a clean finish (soft, with air left, centered on the road).
A pilot written by hand shows that both stunts can be flown
Before training anything, we wanted to know that both stunts can be flown with these five commands. So we wrote a pilot by hand: a few dozen lines of if-then rules that read the same telemetry and send commands through the same 0.2 s interface. On the kickflip, for example, it starts climbing when the truck is 1.1 s away, starts the roll once the car is 1.4 m above the truck's roof, leans against any sideways drift, and lands once the car is past the truck.

ai_industry.title: Canva Chases AI Domination With a New AI Image Model for Designers
ai_industry.summary_original: Canva Craft won’t be the company’s last AI tool. Will creators jump on board?
ai_industry.content_original:
Canva is going deeper down the AI rabbit hole with the release of its first proprietary AI image model, called Canva Craft. It’s now available globally to all Canva users and is made specifically for designers.
This isn’t the first time Canva has added AI, to be sure. The beginner-friendly design program has been adding AI tools and third-party AI models for years. Its first take on creative AI, Magic Media, debuted in 2023. But Canva’s head of AI research, Stefano Corazza, told CNET that the company’s acquisition of Leonardo.Ai and internal ramp-up of AI research helped bolster its efforts to create its own AI image model, one made specifically for designers. Keeping all the AI tech in-house also helps the company keep cloud costs down and inference time quicker, Corazza said.
Canva Craft is meant for designers, and a big part of that is how the model actually works. The model has a two-stage architecture, the company said in a blog post. That means the model, combined with Canva’s behind-the-scenes prompt-improvement tools, can “reason” before generating a design. The model is trained on Canva’s library, licensed and public databases, and data from Canva users who opted in to training, Corazza said. The result is, ideally, more complex and comprehensive designs.
More from CNET
“[The AI] can actually create a whole plan for how the image is going to look like, all the layout. If you think about designers, that’s exactly what they do right when they create a design,” said Corazza. Designers carefully place elements to create a story. “Our model does basically the exact same thing. So we are mimicking exactly the design process.”
Early benchmarking results are positive. On DesignArena, Canva Craft is in fourth place overall for image models, trailing only OpenAI’s ChatGPT Images and beating bigwigs like Google’s Nano Banana and Microsoft’s MAI-Image models. Canva also ranks highly for generating portraits and product-focused imagery, though it trails in the marketing subcategory, which is where a lot of people use Canva.
The ability to edit AI outputs is a priority for Canva, and it’s an important one for anyone who uses AI tools. Often, no matter how perfect your AI prompt is, an image or video generator will spit out a result that is almost, but not quite, right. Canva has been tackling this problem with tools like its Magic Layers, which let you break down an AI design into its most basic elements and adjust them, a technologically complex process that solves a big problem for AI enthusiasts. Canva Craft builds on that foundation and lets you edit results.
Creative controversy
Creative AI tools are controversial, to put it mildly. Photographers, illustrators and artists have been calling out concerns for years about how AI is allegedly trained on their work in violation of copyright protections, used to create abusive material and being offered up to executives as a replacement for real artists. Creative companies from Adobe to Canva have maintained that AI is just a tool they want to offer their creators.
In an apt analogy of the current state of generative media, Eric Wittman, CEO of the popular photo editing and sharing platform VSCO, replied to Canva CEO Melanie Perkins’ LinkedIn post about Canva Craft and said that real photographers, not AI, will always rank No. 1 for portraits.
While executives argue over the best way to incorporate AI, photographers have to deal with AI headaches on every design platform, including VSCO. As AI models improve, it’s also forcing real creators to consistently verify their work as human-made, not AI-generated. But digital verification methods are sporadic, creating an even more complex web for creators to navigate.

ai_industry.content_original:
Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, bringing enhancements to Siri AI, adding Suggestions in Messages, and sneaking in a string of smaller additions across Photos, Podcasts, Games, Apple TV, and FaceTime.
iOS 27.2 is available to download to your device now via Settings ➝ General ➝ Software Update. Note that some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. Apple maintains a feature availability list with all the details.
Ask Siri About Past Conversations
Siri AI can now recall your past conversations, so you can ask it about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week. Siri AI features require an iPhone 16 model or later, or an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max.
Get Answers From More of Your Personal Context
Siri AI can now draw from more sources when answering, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, and your voicemails. Apple says you'll also get better results from Safari history and Reading List.
Use Siri in More Languages
Siri AI now supports French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, in addition to English. Just keep in mind that, as things stand, it's not available in the EU or mainland China.
Control Which Apps Siri and Search Can Access
A new settings menu has been added that lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one list. You can find it in Settings ➝ Siri ➝ Excluded Apps.
Copy Just Part of a Siri Response
Granular text selection lets you select and copy only the part of a Siri response you need, rather than the whole reply.
Act on Suggestions in Messages
The new Suggestions in Messages feature aims to help you take quick actions based on the context of a conversation, like adding a Calendar invite for a dinner or saving a Reminder. The feature appeared during iOS 27 beta testing but was held back from the initial release, so its arrival has been a good while coming.
Manage Shared Albums More Easily
Shared Albums in Photos gain three additions. You can now edit captions and comments, the app can avoid adding duplicate photos, and it can display a reminder before an album expires so participants can save important photos and videos.
Spot AI-Generated Images
iOS 27.2 supports SynthID watermarking, which aims to help you identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground.
See What Your Friends Are Playing
In the Games app, the Friends tab now provides context around friend suggestions, plus it shows you any recent games your friends have played on their player pages.
Create Apple TV Profiles for Your Household
If you have an Apple TV, you can now create profiles in the account settings section on iPhone and iPad. All you need for a profile is a name, plus whether it's for an adult or a child. Creating a profile for a child limits content to a PG rating by default, but there's a customize option for finer control. You can select age ratings for TV shows and movies that are appropriate for the child based on their age.
Stream FaceTime From Front and Rear Cameras
Dual Capture is now available in group FaceTime calls, so you can stream FaceTime video content from the front and rear cameras at the same time. On a compatible device running iOS 27.2, flipping the camera while on a FaceTime call automatically turns on Dual Capture.
Dual Capture is available on the iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.
Watch Several Live Sports Streams at Once
Multiview has been expanded in the Apple TV app to the iPhone, so you can now watch up to four live sports streams at the same time. Multiview works for sports events that come with an Apple TV subscription, so that's Major League Soccer (MLS), Formula 1 (F1) in the U.S., and Friday Night Baseball doubleheaders during the Major League Baseball season.
iPhone Duo Edge Light and Apple Pencil Support
iOS 27.2 adds Apple Pencil USB-C support to the iPhone Duo. It also includes support for the Edge Light feature that first appeared in macOS to illuminate your face during video calls.
Be Reminded of a Contact's Anniversary on a Call
A new feature of Call Context reminds you that it's your anniversary when you call that special person – as long as you've added the date in the Contacts app. To add an anniversary to a contact, open the Contacts app and select their name. Tap "Edit" in the corner, then tap "add date," and the first suggestion under date is anniversary. Do it now. It could save your marriage...

ai_industry.title: Google Debuts New AI Models, Genie 4 and Gemini 4 Carbon: What You Need to Know
ai_industry.summary_original: The world model has a waitlist and the newest frontier Gemini model is restricted to select cybersecurity experts.
ai_industry.content_original:
Google is back with another new frontier AI model, just two weeks after its last release. The new large language model is dubbed Gemini 4 Carbon, the company announced on Wednesday. And if you’re a fan of world models, there’s good news there, too: Google’s latest, Genie 4, also debuted this week.
Gemini 4 Carbon is the most advanced the company has released. It surpassed its own Gemini 4 Argon model and competitors like OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on benchmarking tests designed to assess a model’s overall capabilities. But Google is pitching the model as one meant for cybersecurity experts. Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is good at detecting and patching vulnerabilities — a skill we’ve already seen can uncover major problems, as with last week’s PHP vulnerabilities affecting a majority of the world’s websites.
Google’s other new AI model this week is Genie 4. This is a world model, which can simulate real and imagined physical worlds. Whereas chatbots predict the next word in a sentence, world models are grounded in the physics of a digital universe. They’re useful for things like robotics and video game design. Genie 4 will introduce a new capability: audio. Developers will be able to add background noise and dialogue to their AI worlds. You may have heard of two AI bigwigs, Fei-Fei Li and Yann LeCun, building world models in their respective start-ups.
More from CNET
Neither of these new models, Gemini 4 Carbon nor Genie 4, is available to the general public yet. Right now, only select cybersecurity experts have access to Gemini 4 Carbon. Google declined to answer a question from CNET about when we can expect access to open up, but if we go by previous releases, it may be as soon as one to two weeks from now. Google says it is actively engaging with the US government’s review process. You can join the waitlist for Genie 4 now.
Google ended 2025 as a major player in the AI industry, but it hasn’t kept up with its peers in the so-called “AI race.” Gemini 4 Argon was the company’s first new frontier model in 11 months — a long time in an industry that sees new models seemingly every week.
But public appetite for AI has changed a lot since 2025. Fears around AI have risen, as has public backlash against AI infrastructure projects such as data centers. While fears about AI contributing to human extinction are often overblown or actually give tech companies more power, other fears about AI leading to mass job losses, misinformation and deepfakes are alive and well.

ai_industry.title: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
ai_industry.summary_original: The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it's sparked some drama among users. NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature last Friday, which can be used to recommend substituti…
ai_industry.content_original:
The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it has sparked some drama among users. Last Friday, NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature, which can be used to recommend substitutions for ingredients and cooking equipment, scale recipes to any number of servings, and “generally make our recipes work for what a cook needs at that moment.”
The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
Some users aren’t exactly thrilled with The New York Times’ recipe-tweaking AI tool.
One of the examples given in the article shows a user asking to use baby spinach instead of kale, with the Cooking app feature advising that because baby spinach wilts faster, it should be added during a later step of the recipe. Ko says it can also change the recipes around different pans and tools. Customized recipes are private and can’t be published or shared through the app. The AI modification feature is being rolled out gradually while the NYT monitors how it performs — it’s currently available to all Cooking subscribers on the iOS app, and it will be more broadly available “soon.”
Some NYT readers have pushed back against the feature, citing concerns in the article’s comment section around the environmental impact of widespread AI adoption and the general impact that AI features may have on the user experience. When one user asked if there will be a way to disable the AI feature, Ko responded with, “No, not at this time,” and noted that the feature is “completely optional to use.”
“Unbelievably disappointing to see,” said another NYT user. “I’ve always loved NYT Cooking and it pains me that the AI mandate has reached what used to be a wonderful and simple collection of recipes and notes from all sorts of different people.”
This isn’t the first time that AI has been used by the NYT Cooking app. Ko says it was used to convert imperial volume measurements to metric weight measurements in recipes two years ago, and a feature was added last year that converts recipes to halve or double the original serving size. The comments on the new AI feature announcement post have since been closed, but NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen tells The Verge that this is standard practice:
“Comments on this article remained open for four days, with editors from Cooking taking care to answer questions, address concerns and engage directly with readers. We kept that conversation open to give readers a meaningful opportunity to share feedback and hear from the team. Closing comments on older articles is standard practice at The Times so that our moderators can focus on new discussions. We’re pleased to see that many members of our Cooking community are interested in exploring this tool and are already trying it out on our iOS app; they’re reporting good results.”

ai_industry.title: Binance hackers stole $6.3 billion in record-breaking crypto heist
ai_industry.summary_original: Binance has disclosed that $6.3 billion worth of crypto funds have been stolen from the platform, in what's believed to be the biggest cryptocurrency hack on record. In a series of updates posted to X, the crypto exchange said that user funds are safe, and th…
ai_industry.content_original:
Binance has disclosed that $6.3 billion worth of crypto funds have been stolen from the platform, in what’s believed to be the biggest cryptocurrency hack on record. In a series of updates posted to X, the crypto exchange said that user funds are safe, and that around $3 billion of the impacted assets have been frozen so far.
Binance hackers stole $6.3 billion in record-breaking crypto heist
$3 billion of stolen assets have been frozen so far, and Binance has promised to ‘cover all losses.’
Binance has publicly committed to covering any losses resulting from the hack. The company has an emergency reserve fund of around $1.3 billion (at last valuation) to protect user assets in these situations, and said it has also reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds to cover this incident — $5 billion of which is “already held in the exact token assets that were impacted.”
“Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach,” Binance reported on X. “This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it.”
The company shared details about the compromised laptop that belongs to one of its DevOps engineers in a prior update, saying it allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. Deposits and withdrawals have been suspended in response to the hack, and the affected address has had its authorization revoked.
“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action. It involved a more complex attack process,” Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual. So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak.”
Binance may not be pointing fingers at who’s behind the attack, but blockchain analysis firms TRM and Chainalysis both attribute it to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime hacking group that has a history of stealing funds from cryptocurrency exchanges. This is the largest known cryptocurrency heist in history — four times higher than the previous record, when $1.46 billion was stolen from Bybit last year — and according to TRM, most of the theft occurred over a period of just 20 minutes.
This isn’t the first time Binance has been hacked, having suffered a previous security breach in 2019 in which $40 million worth of crypto assets (valued at the time) were stolen. The latest hack comes as cases of large-scale crypto theft are escalating, however, after several heists were disclosed by crypto companies in September. There are also new concerns around how AI tools can be used maliciously against the industry, with OpenAI reporting earlier this month that one of its models managed to swipe fake crypto on an Ethereum test network it didn’t have access to.
“This is an extraordinary hack, for its size and for the response... Few financial systems have ever shown a theft of this scale,” TRM chief policy officer Ari Redbord said in a statement to Sky News. “The theft shows how exposed the system is to sophisticated attackers moving at a speed we have never seen.”

ai_industry.content_original:
清华姚期智团队新作：代数世界模型，让AI像牛顿一样思考
让AI像牛顿一样思考
Jay发自 凹非寺 量子位|公众号QbitAI
「让AI像牛顿一样思考」，这件事，终于有望了。
清华大学姚期智和袁洋老师领导的科研团队，搞出了一个重磅项目，叫「代数世界模型」（Algebraic World Model,AWM）。
之前大家老爱问一个问题：
如果让AI只学习牛顿发现万有引力之前的所有知识，它能自己把万有引力给推导出来吗？
尴尬的是，训练数据容易被污染，很难复原出这样的情景：打造一个完全陌生的世界，让AI从0开始观察和实验。
但如今，代数世界模型给出了一种新解法。让AI从观察和实验出发，进一步理解世界这件事，变得没那么遥远了。
AI玩游戏，像不像第谷观星？
有个叫ARC-AGI-3的游戏集，现在是各大前沿模型秀肌肉的地方。这游戏的特点就是，啥也不告诉你，没有规则，没有目标。
就是单纯的，让你自己去摸索。
像GPT Astra这种顶流选手，配合Provider Adapter框架，在这里面能拿到99.9%的高分。
它在玩游戏的时候，会自己把游戏机制整理成一堆符号化的规则。
密密麻麻，信息密度是很高，比其他模型精确多了。
但本质上，这东西就像是第谷的实验记录本。
第谷，开普勒的老师，一个观测狂人，记录了巨量的行星运行数据，精确得吓人。
但他也只是记录现象。
真正从这些数据里，发现行星运动三大定律，揭示背后本质规律的，是开普勒。
Astra生成的这些规则，就是第谷的笔记本，不是开普勒的定律。它只描述了现象，没抓住这个迷你游戏世界运行的本质。
仍然会有「幻觉」
只记录现象，会出什么问题呢？
研究人员把其中一个叫sc25的游戏，稍微改了改，初始步数设置成了一个根本不可能通关的数字。
比如第四关，本来起码要19步才能赢，他们就只给你18步。
然后让Astra去玩。
结果，Astra试了8轮，有点沮丧，然后断言：18步肯定不行，我估计至少要22步才能赢。
是的，它不仅没发现正确答案，还给出了一个错得离谱的22步。
这还不是个例。在12次类似的测试里，顶级的GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 5.5加起来，只有5次判断出「不可能」，其中4次给出的最低步数还是错的。
这种幻觉在游戏里，最多就是坑你一下。
但如果在现实世界里，让一个AI智能体去执行任务，它告诉你「这事儿没戏」，还给个错误的原因，那后果可能就严重了。
我们真正需要的，是AI在任务不可能时，能清楚地告诉我们「为什么不可能」，并且给出准确的判断，比如「只要条件再增加一点点，就可能了」。
很明显，光靠直觉和试错是不行的。
代数的力量
怎么解决？
这时候，就得靠代数的力量了。也就是前面提到的，清华团队搞的那个代数世界模型（AWM）。
把游戏里的所有对象、关系和规则，抽象成一个「代数世界」。然后，利用大模型现在已经超强的数学能力，去理解这个世界。
过程大概是三步：
- 探索：先玩几下，把看到的现象写成可执行的Python代码，作为初步的「假设」或「规律」。
- 凝炼：用新的观察去验证、修正这些假设，然后把它们提炼成更通用的对象和规则。
- 证明：最后，把这些规律形式化成一种叫Lean 4的语言，变成逻辑严密、机器可以自动检查的数学断言。
说白了，从探索试错走向建模和形式化证明。
效果怎么样呢？
面对刚才那个无解的关卡，基于Opus 5.5模型的AWM，只需要尝试两次，就能直接证明，这关在当前步数下就是无解的，而且只需要再多一步就能获胜。
除了能判断「不可能」，AWM通关的能力也更强。在整个ARC-AGI-3测试集里，它用Opus 5，183个关卡全部通关，得分99.9%，同时，平均通关的动作数，只有人类基准的43%。
是目前所有已知系统里，效率最高的。
那AWM具体是怎么实现的呢？
大家可能之前听说过代数几何，代数拓扑。简单来说，代数几何把代数方程与几何形状联系起来，代数拓扑则用代数工具研究空间的连接、孔洞等性质。
通过把形状和空间代数化，可以解决许多单凭观察难以回答的问题。数学家创造了代数几何和代数拓扑，那是因为几何和拓扑就是他们关注的世界。
而现在，借助AI的力量，AWM可以把这条道路延伸到更多陌生的游戏、交互环境乃至现实任务中：从探索中发现规律，从规律中凝炼结构，再借助数学理解这些结构。
像牛顿一样思考
这背后的思路，其实贯穿了整个科学史。
从万有引力、麦克斯韦方程组到相对论，人类最顶尖的智慧，一直在做一件事：从复杂的现象中，提炼出最基本的规律，用数学这个统一的语言来描述世界。
AWM想做的，就是让AI也学会这套方法。
为了实现这个目标，它从一个叫「范畴论」的数学分支里找了灵感。这玩意儿听着特吓人，号称是「数学的数学」，因为它研究的不是某个具体的数学领域，而是不同数学理论背后的共同结构。
AWM主要用了里面的两个工具，叫「投射极限」和「归纳极限」，本质上就是两种互补的思维方式：
- 下定义（投射极限）：把一堆已有的概念和它们的关系拼在一起，共同定义一个新东西。你可以理解成概念的分解和组合。
- 找共性（归纳极限）：观察一堆不同的东西，找到它们之间的共同点，然后把它们统一到一个更抽象的框架里。你可以理解成概念的泛化和特化。
通过这两种方式来回倒腾，AWM就能把一开始那些零散、混乱的Python假设，不断迭代，变得越来越简洁、清晰、一致，最终形成一个可以推理和证明的世界模型。
想想牛顿当年，他面对的也不是一道写好了答案的题，而是无数零散的观测数据和现象。真正伟大的工作，是从这些现象中，找到「力」、「质量」这些少数核心概念，再把它们组织成一个可以推演、可以检验的理论体系。
AWM想教给AI的，就是这种工作方式。
当然，它也有边界。它的证明，是基于它「观测到的世界」成立的。如果探索得不够全面，遗漏了某些关键规则，那这个模型描绘的也只是一个「局部真理」，而不是完整的世界。
所以，真正的路径是一个不断循环的过程：
观察→假设→实验→抽象→证明→再观察
